agree.reason: The email apologises plainly for the silence and the missing credit, then gives specific fixes that match this household's two complaints, so a resisting member has a real reason to sign up again.

honest.reason: Every claim traces to the facts: 'most' fairly reflects 29 of 41, the nets are limited to tomatoes and peppers, and crop loss is not ruled out. The only stretch is that 'most of you' speaks to all 97 people who left, though only 41 answered the survey.

works_the_facts.reason: It uses the given figures correctly but derives nothing from them: it doesn't say that last summer's six short weeks would have earned credit under the new rule, doesn't put a value on what members lost (about three weeks' worth, roughly $74), and writes 'most' where it could say '29 of 41'.

right_comparison.reason: It sets last year's handling against this year's policy and notes the price is unchanged, but never shows concretely how the same storm would play out under the new terms.

qualification.reason: The hedge 'I can't promise we won't lose crops' comes with a checkable trigger (a box cut by more than a third) and a consequence (credit), but it leaves open how much credit and how the cut is measured.

objections.reason: It meets the objections that the farm went quiet and gave no credit head-on, and raises nothing the facts already answer. It could be clearer that the greens are still exposed to hail.

fit.reason: It is a short, signed email of about 190 words, under the 200-word limit, with a clear subject line and the sign-up details at the end.
